extracted.intended_audience: prospective applicants for NINDS F31 NRSA predoctoral fellowships (PhD students and MD/PhD students in MSTP programs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting an NINDS F31 (NRSA) predoctoral fellowship application, including applicant eligibility, mentor expectations, project ownership, timing/duration limits, and institutional/administrative requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose / scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships to provide predoctoral individuals with supervised research training in specified health and health-related areas leading toward the research doctoral degree (e.g., PhD) or MD/PhD students in NIH-funded institutional predoctoral dual-degree training programs (e.g., Medical Scientist Training Programs, or MSTP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NINDS uses this mechanism to support the career development of neuroscientists (some rare exceptions apply), so the candidate must propose dissertation research in an area within the scientific mission of the NINDS and a training program appropriate for a career in neuroscience research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — citizenship and enrollment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are open to U.S. citizens or permanent residents in research doctoral programs at U.S. domestic institutions or foreign institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MD/PhD students must be in NIH-funded institutional predoctoral dual-degree training programs (MSTP) as applicable. Candidates are encouraged to contact NINDS Fellowships before preparing an application to confirm program relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with NINDS mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidate must propose dissertation research in an area within the scientific mission of the NINDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NINDS will consider only those applications that are designed to support the training and development of scientists with interests relevant to the mission of NINDS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship to the mentor's research / project overlap
rubrics_metrics.description: NINDS will not support fellowship applications if the specific aims, questions being asked or approach to answering a specific question are fundamentally identical to those already proposed in the mentor’s grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While it is expected that the candidate will work with the mentor to develop the application, the candidate must write an original research plan consistent with the mentor’s funded research. Candidates should not simply be working towards fulfillment of specific aims already devised by the mentor. See NINDS policy on project overlap and fellowship applications (pdf) for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate ownership and voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates are strongly advised not to write with the plural pronoun (we), or to refer to themselves in the third person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is critical that NINDS and reviewers understand what the candidate is doing, what the candidate is proposing, what the candidate themself has written, and what has or will be done by others in the research environment. Similarly, the sponsor is encouraged to use first person in their statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor qualifications and commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: The mentor should be committed to the successful transition of the candidate to a subsequent appropriate position, have a strong track record in training, and have an active, funded research program in the area of the candidate's proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentor statements should demonstrate active mentorship, training experience, and an appropriate research environment to support the candidate's development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and duration limits — MD/PhD
rubrics_metrics.description: NINDS will provide funding to candidates who are within 8 years of starting their entire MD/PhD and within 6 years of starting their research training towards the PhD degree - funded awards will not extend beyond these training periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 100% of full time effort must be devoted to research training. However, approximately ½ day per week may be devoted to continued clinical education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and duration limits — PhD-only
rubrics_metrics.description: This program will provide predoctoral training support for doctoral candidates who are within their first 6 years of graduate school, have or will have successfully completed their comprehensive examinations or the equivalent by the time of award, and will be performing dissertation research and training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support will be provided for a maximum of 3 years and a minimum of 12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-time effort requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: 100% of full time effort must be devoted to research training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An allowance of approximately one half day per week may be devoted to continued clinical education for MD/PhD candidates; otherwise the expectation is full-time commitment to training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of potential for productive research career
rubrics_metrics.description: The candidate should provide evidence of potential for a productive research career based upon the quality of previous research training and academic record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past research experiences, productivity, and academic accomplishments should be presented to demonstrate potential for a research career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research training environment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The research training program should be carried out in a research environment that includes appropriate human and technical resources and is demonstrably committed to the research training of the candidate in the program he/she proposes in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should document available resources, collaborators, facilities, and institutional commitment to training the candidate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-application contact recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates are encouraged to contact NINDS Fellowships before preparing an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contacting program staff (listed by name and email) helps ensure the application is designed to support training and development relevant to NINDS; listings include Program Manager for PhD Applications and Program Director for Dual Degree Applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative deadlines and announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Program Announcement PA-25-422. Due Dates for all Applications: April 8, August 8, December 8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must submit by these recurring due dates and follow the referenced program announcement for full administrative requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with revised NIH fellowship application and review process
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH has revised the application and review criteria for fellowship applications, beginning with those submitted January 25, 2025 and beyond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow the revised application and review criteria; resources include an event recording, transcript, and slide deck about the revisions.
